objective: Provide a secure password-reset link for any account, including an account whose email address has not yet been verified, without changing email verification state.
acceptance_criteria: Start gate: a human-approved Director prerequisite has configured an approved transactional email sender, narrowly scoped permission to send its messages and Cognito AdminGetUser/AdminSetUserPassword/AdminUserGlobalSignOut permissions for this pool; the human has approved the Cognito Essentials or Plus plan and PasswordHistorySize=1 because FeaturePlan.LITE does not provide password-history enforcement. No AWS write or plan upgrade is part of this task.

Start gate: a Director-owned policy/scope PR has made the specific backend/alembic/versions/** migration path writable to the code agent and merged before this task starts. The task worker does not change .ai/policy.json.

The sign-in page retains an accessible Forgot password link below the password field. Its request page contains one labelled email input and a confirm button; the reset link opens a separate new-password page with labelled New password and Confirm password inputs.

For every syntactically valid request, known and unknown addresses receive the same success status, body and user-facing message with no account-existence or delivery detail. Response timing does not disclose account existence. The server sends a link only to the address associated with the matching Cognito account, including when that address is unverified.
Requests are rate-limited by normalized account address and source IP to at most 5 requests per hour per key. Unknown, disabled and unverified-account cases do not reveal which case occurred.

The server generates at least 256 bits of cryptographically secure reset-token entropy, stores only a one-way token hash bound to the Cognito subject, and expires it after 30 minutes. A reset token is single-use; issuing a new token invalidates outstanding tokens for the account. At most 5 invalid token submissions are accepted per token before it is invalidated.

Reset URLs use HTTPS and a configured allowlisted origin, never the request Host header. The raw token is not written to application logs, analytics, telemetry, server request logs, or third-party referrers; the reset page uses Referrer-Policy: no-referrer and sends no third-party requests. Tokens are removed from the visible URL before rendering the form.

The server changes the Cognito password only after validating and atomically consuming the reset token. It does not set email_verified or otherwise verify the email as a side effect. Cognito enforces the configured password policy and rejects reuse of the current password through PasswordHistorySize=1; the application never compares, stores or logs a plaintext current password.

New password and confirmation must match before submission. A mismatch is an accessible field error and makes no request. Invalid, expired, consumed, or exhausted tokens fail without changing the password and without identifying an account.

A successful reset persists one durable server-side valid-after row keyed by Cognito subject, independent of whether a local profile row exists; the row outlives reset-token records and is updated on every successful reset. Every locally JWT-validated API request checks the verified ID token's auth_time against this persistent barrier; tokens with auth_time at or before the reset cutoff receive 401. The barrier check fails closed if its state cannot be read. The cutoff accounts for Cognito auth_time's one-second precision so pre-reset tokens cannot pass; document any brief reauthentication delay caused by rounding.

After the barrier is durable, the reset flow calls Cognito AdminUserGlobalSignOut to stop refresh-token sessions, sends a password-change notice to the account email, includes no password in the email, and requires normal sign-in; it does not automatically create an authenticated session. A successful reset is not reported until the password update, barrier persistence, and global sign-out have succeeded.

Users depends on the injected EmailSender interface only; it imports no notification concrete class, SES adapter, Notification model/table, or preference. The interface's security-email operation delivers transactional security mail without creating an in-app notification, and its test double is covered by backend/tests/notifications/test_email.py.

Tests cover known/unknown account response equivalence, unverified account delivery, rate limits, token expiry/replay/hash-only persistence, URL/log/referrer leakage, mismatch, password reuse rejection, valid-after rejection of pre-reset ID tokens on locally JWT-validated API requests (including a Cognito subject without a profile), failure-closed barrier lookup, global sign-out, and no email_verified mutation. Local browser rows use localhost and a human-controlled dev-pool address; report evidence or NOT DONE.
No new dependency. The relevant Users and Frontend module references record the flow and its security boundary.
